approachQuestion.prompt:
Locate the longest even-handed segment

Input: a binary array votes. Return the maximum length of a contiguous segment containing equally many zeroes and ones. Return 0 when no nonempty such segment exists.

Example 1: votes = [1,1,0,1,0,0,1]. Output: 6, for indices 0 through 5. Example 2: votes = [1,1]. Output: 0. Example 3: votes = []. Output: 0. 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; each entry is 0 or 1.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Treat zero as −1 and one as +1 while scanning a running balance. Start with balance 0 at prefix position 0. Map each balance to its earliest prefix position; on repeats maximize the distance to that earliest position.
options.feedback: Equal balances delimit exactly balanced segments. The earliest matching prefix maximizes the length for each right boundary.

options.text: Store every prefix position in a list for its balance, then take the largest last-position minus first-position across the lists.
options.feedback: This is correct, but the intermediate lists retain all positions unnecessarily; only the earliest position and current scan position are needed for each balance.

options.text: Keep only the latest prefix position for each balance and maximize distances to those latest positions.
options.feedback: For [1,0,1,0], balance 0 repeats at prefix positions 0,2,4. Replacing 0 by 2 loses the full length 4.

options.text: Use a window that shrinks immediately whenever its counts of zeroes and ones differ.
options.feedback: A temporary imbalance may later cancel. For [1,1,0,0], discarding an imbalanced prefix prevents discovering the full balanced length 4.

feedback.reason: Retain the earliest occurrence of a repeated prefix state when the objective maximizes interval length.
details: Scan votes without constructing a transformed array. Maintain a scalar balance, adding −1 for zero and +1 for one. Initialize a map with balance 0→prefix position 0. At each later prefix position, maximize the distance if the balance was seen; otherwise store this position and never overwrite it.
For [1,0,1,0], balance zero occurs at boundaries 0,2,4. Keeping boundary 0 allows length four; replacing it with boundary 2 loses the longest candidate.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Locate the longest even-handed segment — analyzed method”, n is array length and b is the number of distinct prefix balances encountered, including the initial zero; b≤n+1. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input for the stated size parameters, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

feedback.reason: Store the earliest index for each distinct prefix balance.
details: Retain the earliest occurrence of a repeated prefix state when the objective maximizes interval length.
Each array entry updates one scalar balance and performs a constant number of expected amortized map operations. Expected O(n+1).
The map stores one earliest position for each of b distinct prefix balances, including the initial zero. There is no transformed copy or list of every prefix position. O(b+1).
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(b + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(1) auxiliary space.”: The map may retain a different prefix balance at every position.
“Expected O(n² + 1) time; O(b + 1) space.”: Matching balances are looked up directly; all segment endpoints are not enumerated.

“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(n + 1) space even when b is bounded, as the tight bound.”: The fixed method stores one earliest index per balance, not every prefix position; the tighter parameterized bound is O(b+1).
